newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Rundown of Albanian flashpoints, rebel-held towns.
newsitem.headline: Rundown of Albanian flashpoints, rebel-held towns.

text.p: Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino has backed the idea of talks with rebels holding towns throughout the south, but unrest is moving closer to Tirana.
At least 10 major towns are in the hands of rebels who have looted military weapons, while other flashpoints have emerged in the past 24 hours.
Here is the situation in Albania on Wednesday.

-- Elbasan. A military base near the town was looted of weapons by civilians from the nearby town of Cerrik. One man was injured in the incident which has brought the southern Albanian revolt to within 55 km (35 miles) of the capital.
-- Cerrik. Two people reported dead from gunshot wounds.
-- Tirana. Men remove arms from the military academy, with secret police and civilians reported to have been involved.
-- Bajram Curri. Up to 300 people loot Kalashnikov assault rifles from a military base in this northern town.

-- Vlore. One person reported dead on Wednesday in Albania's second largest Adriatic port, effectively seized in early February by residents furious at the loss of their savings in the failed Gjallica pyramid investment scheme.
-- Sarande. Smaller port and resort town further south, opposite the Greek holiday island of Corfu. The town is one of the centres for Albania's ethnic Greek community.
-- Delvine. Sixteen km (10 miles) inland from Sarande. A small town which fell to the rebels in the same wave that brought the two ports under insurgent control.

-- Tepelene. A remote mountain town of 20,000 on the main road south to Greece. It is the site of a top-security prison which held Socialist party leader Fatos Nano, jailed on corruption charges in 1994. He was moved to Tirana before the insurgents took control of the town last week and set up big artillery guns in the central square.
-- Memaliaj. A small town between Tepelene and Fieri, known as a coal area. The bridge over the Vjose river in the town has been blocked since last month.

-- Gjirokaster. An ancient town and centre of the ethnic Greek community, only 30 km (20 miles) from the Greek border. Rebels overran the town and raided a big military barracks on Saturday after a government attempt to fly in troops.
-- Permet. Rebels took control of this remote town on Sunday and vowed not to surrender until Berisha resigned. Five people were killed and six injured in the fighting.

-- Berat. One of Albania's oldest towns, where rioting broke out in January over lost savings in pyramid schemes. Rebels seized control of the town at the weekend. Hospital sources said one person had been killed and 20 slightly injured in random shooting, but there were no clashes.
-- Kucove. An oil refinery area, near Berat where rebels controlled 19 MiG fighters after pillaging an air force base, one of two important military airfields in Albania.
-- Corovode. A remote town at the site of Tomorri mountain, 50 km (30 miles) south of Berat. Chosen by the late Stalinist leader Enver Hoxha as Albania's capital in case of war.
-- Polican. A small town between Corovode and Berat where there is a military plant producing Kalashnikov rifles.
-- Gramsh. This small town in central Albania, 96 km (58 miles) southeast of Tirana is believed to have fallen into rebel hands.
